root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Orthodox Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 d5 4. Nc3 Be7 5. Bg5 O-O 6. e3 Nbd7

overview: Black builds a compact set-up with ...Be7, ...O-O and ...Nbd7 and aims for ...c6, ...dxc4 and ...e5. White usually plays 7.Rc1, 7.Qc2 or 7.Bd3 (Botvinnik), or the Exchange, and tries for a small space edge, in the Carlsbad structure if cxd5 exd5.

white_ideas.idea: cxd5 and the minority attack in the Carlsbad structure
Rc1 and Qc2, e4 break when Black has exchanged on c4

black_ideas.idea: Hold d5 and e6 and trade down, waiting for ...c5 or ...e5

typical_structures.structure: Tense QGD centre with pawns on d4/e3 against d5/e6

character.notes: Orthodox QGD is the textbook solid defence: few weaknesses, steady play.

gambit.notes: No gambit; the Queen's Gambit is not one.

structure.notes: Centre in tension or Carlsbad after an exchange; flexible.

approach.notes: A main-line Queen's Gambit defence, standard.

level.notes: Anchor: Intermediate; plans matter more than long theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Rubinstein 7.Qc2 c6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 Nbd7 7. Qc2 c6
sublines_that_differ.how: Same set-up with a different White queen square.

character.reason: Anchor: Orthodox Defense is hard to break down.

structure.reason: QGD centre in tension; Carlsbad after exchanges.

approach.reason: A main-line defence, not a universal set-up.

plans.reason: The typical White plan after the exchange.
